extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and journalists seeking information about a satirical/fake-news website
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing the Dunning–Kruger Times, an American satirical online newspaper, its network affiliation, disclaimers, and history of being fact-checked/debunked by major outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical online newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dunning–Kruger Times is a satirical online newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the publication's genre as satire rather than factual reporting; sets reader expectation that content is not intended as literal news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is part of a network of websites run by America's Last Line of Defense, with a writer in the state of Maine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates organizational provenance and shared practices/style across related sites; useful when assessing the site's credibility or patterns of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published disclaimer: 'nothing on this page is real'
rubrics_metrics.description: All of which state 'nothing on this page is real'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explicit disclaimer is an editorial practice signaling satirical intent; when evaluating individual items, presence of this statement should be taken as a cue that stories are not factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of being debunked by fact-checkers and press
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories published by Dunning-Kruger have been debunked by Snopes.com, USA Today, Reuters, the Associated Press, and by The Guardian and The Houston Chronicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing claims originating from the site, consult fact-checking outlets listed; the site's content has a documented pattern of being mistaken for real news and subsequently debunked.
